scenes.tts: How does a sugar added to a protein inside its E R end up outside the cell? No vesicle ever carries it across a membrane.
scenes.caption: How does a sugar added to a protein inside its ER end up outside the cell? No vesicle ever carries it across a membrane.
scenes.visual: WORLD for the whole film (schematic, label 'schematic' at size 28 in a corner): one cell cross-section filling ~85% of frame height. Plasma membrane = thick grey double line (two lipid sheets) around the frame edge; beyond it a teal-tinted band labelled 'outside'. Inside, at left, the ER drawn as a long closed sac (grey double-line wall, teal-tinted interior); centre, a Golgi as three stacked closed sacs, teal interiors; the space between organelles is the cytosol, tinted soft gold, with slow drifting gold specks (updater, never stops). Carried object: 'the protein', a blue bar spanning a membrane, a yellow ball 'N' on one end, a green ball 'C' on the other; the sugar is an orange labelled flag 'sugar' on a short stem from the blue bar near the N ball. Every lumen on the secretory and endocytic routes and the outside stay teal; the cytosol stays gold, all film. Open already on the cell, zoomed toward the ER. The protein sits in the ER wall, N ball in the teal ER lumen, C ball in the gold cytosol. On 'sugar added' the orange sugar flag grows from the blue bar beside the N ball. Camera eases out to the whole cell during 'inside its E R'. On 'outside the cell' a ghost orange flag pulses on the outer face of the plasma membrane, and a dashed orange line starts drawing from the ER sugar toward it. On 'across a membrane' the dashed line reaches the ER wall and a red X flashes where it would cross; the dashed line keeps flickering, a big '?' rises beside the ghost flag.
scenes.narration: How does a sugar added to a protein inside its ER end up outside the cell? No vesicle ever carries it across a membrane.

scenes.visual: Title 'Which Side Is Outside?' fades in over the dimmed cell (gold specks still drifting) for 2 s, then dissolves; the cell stays.

scenes.tts: Every membrane here is two sheets of lipid, so it has two faces. One face always touches the cytosol, the fluid around the organelles. The other face touches either the outside of the cell, or a lumen, the space inside an organelle.
scenes.visual: Camera pushes into a stretch of the ER wall until the double line fills the frame as two horizontal sheets (rows of small grey head dots, tails as short lines; schematic, no lipid structures). On 'two sheets' each sheet brightens in turn and slow lateral jitter runs through the head dots. On 'two faces' two arrows sweep along the top and bottom surfaces. On 'touches the cytosol' the gold side below pulses and gets the label 'cytosol'. On 'outside of the cell' the camera briefly glides to the plasma membrane where the teal side is labelled 'outside'; on 'a lumen' it glides back to the ER and the teal side is labelled 'lumen'. Gold specks drift throughout.
scenes.narration: Every membrane here is two sheets of lipid, so it has two faces. One face always touches the cytosol, the fluid around the organelles. The other face touches either the outside of the cell, or a lumen, the space inside an organelle.

scenes.tts: Every space touching a cytosol face is gold. Every lumen on these routes, and the outside, is teal. On these routes, each membrane has one gold face and one teal face.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to the whole cell. A brush-like wipe re-paints the cytosol gold across the frame on 'is gold'; on 'is teal' the ER lumen, each Golgi sac and the outside band flash teal one after another, left to right. On 'one gold face and one teal face' a thin gold edge and a thin teal edge trace around every membrane at once, like two coloured outlines running laps. The outlines keep running to the end of the scene.
scenes.narration: Every space touching a cytosol face is gold. Every lumen on these routes, and the outside, is teal. On these routes, each membrane has one gold face and one teal face.

scenes.tts: A patch of the plasma membrane dimples inward and pinches off as a sac. Predict: what fills the sac, and which face touches the cytosol?
scenes.visual: Zoom to the lower plasma membrane. On 'dimples inward' the membrane curves in slowly, a teal pocket of outside fluid forming; on 'pinches off' the neck closes and a small round sac floats into the gold cytosol. Its interior stays teal, but a neutral translucent veil marked '?' overlays it after scission; do not recolor the contents. On 'Predict' a question card slides in at top right: 'Contents? Which face meets cytosol?' The sac drifts slowly.
scenes.narration: A patch of the plasma membrane dimples inward and pinches off as a sac. Predict: what fills the sac, and which face touches the cytosol?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause: the question card stays on screen; the veiled sac bobs gently in the cytosol and gold specks drift. No new labels.

scenes.tts: It holds a gulp of outside fluid, so its lumen is teal. The gold face still touches the cytosol. Nothing crossed a membrane. It only changed shape.
scenes.visual: Question card fades. On 'outside fluid' the neutral veil clears to reveal the teal contents. On 'gold face' the outer edge of the sac glows gold toward the cytosol. On 'Nothing crossed' a replay plays at half size beside it: the dimple-and-pinch runs again, with the teal and gold outlines staying on their own sides throughout. On 'changed shape' the replay loops once more.
scenes.narration: It holds a gulp of outside fluid, so its lumen is teal. The gold face still touches the cytosol. Nothing crossed a membrane. It only changed shape.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. On these routes, lumens count as outside because budding and fusing connect them without crossing a membrane.
scenes.visual: Banner across the top builds word by word with the narration: 'route lumens = outside'. Under it, show topology as a sequence of transformations, not as a simultaneous tunnel through closed compartments. First the outside band dimples around a teal dot; the sac pinches off and then fuses with an endosome. Separately, run the reverse sequence from ER to Golgi to a secretory vesicle and the outside. The dot always stays in teal space and never crosses a grey line. Draw a short teal trail only while two spaces are physically connected.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. On these routes, lumens count as outside because budding and fusing connect them without crossing a membrane.

scenes.tts: So where does a protein get its direction? It is normally set once, at the E R, as the chain is made. A channel called the translocon threads one end into the lumen.
scenes.caption: So where does a protein get its direction? It is normally set once, at the ER, as the chain is made. A channel called the translocon threads one end into the lumen.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the ER wall. A ribosome cartoon (labelled block 'ribosome') sits on the gold side over a labelled grey channel block 'translocon' in the wall. On 'as the chain is made' a blue-yellow chain feeds out of the ribosome; on 'threads one end into the lumen' the yellow N end pushes through the translocon into the teal lumen and the blue spanning segment slides sideways out of the channel into the wall. Chain keeps feeding while the narrator speaks.
scenes.narration: So where does a protein get its direction? It is normally set once, at the ER, as the chain is made. A channel called the translocon threads one end into the lumen.

scenes.tts: Here the N terminus goes into the lumen, and the C terminus stays in the cytosol. That is called type one. In the lumen, an enzyme adds the sugar to the N terminal region.
scenes.caption: Here the N terminus goes into the lumen, and the C terminus stays in the cytosol. That is called type I. In the lumen, an enzyme adds the sugar to the N-terminal region.
scenes.visual: The protein finishes: green C ball pops out on the gold side. On 'N terminus' the yellow N ball pulses on the teal side; on 'C terminus' the green C ball pulses on the gold side. On 'type one' a label 'type I' slides in beside it. On 'an enzyme adds the sugar' a labelled block 'sugar-adding enzyme' glides along the teal face of the wall and the orange sugar flag grows from the blue protein beside the N ball.
scenes.narration: Here the N terminus goes into the lumen, and the C terminus stays in the cytosol. That is called type I. In the lumen, an enzyme adds the sugar to the N-terminal region.

scenes.visual: Show before tell: camera eases back from the ER wall to ER plus Golgi; the ER wall around the protein starts to bulge into the gold cytosol (the bud begins). Gold specks drift.

scenes.tts: A vesicle buds from the E R and fuses with the Golgi. Its lumen joins first the E R lumen, then the Golgi lumen. The sugar never leaves teal.
scenes.caption: A vesicle buds from the ER and fuses with the Golgi. Its lumen joins first the ER lumen, then the Golgi lumen. The sugar never leaves teal.
scenes.visual: Camera pulls back to ER and Golgi. The bud begun in the previous beat pinches off on 'buds': a vesicle (teal inside) with the protein in its wall, N and sugar inside, C outside on the gold side. The vesicle glides across the cytosol during 'and fuses with the Golgi', and on 'fuses' its wall merges with the first Golgi sac; the teal interiors join with a ripple. On 'never leaves teal' the sugar flag glows and a teal trail behind it shows its whole route stayed inside teal space; the green C ball stays on gold the whole time.
scenes.narration: A vesicle buds from the ER and fuses with the Golgi. Its lumen joins first the ER lumen, then the Golgi lumen. The sugar never leaves teal.

scenes.visual: Show before tell: a new vesicle carrying the protein (N and sugar inside, C on gold) buds from the last Golgi sac and starts drifting up through the cytosol toward the plasma membrane.

scenes.tts: A secretory vesicle then fuses with the plasma membrane. Its lumen opens to the outside. The sugar now faces the fluid around the cell. It rode inside a lumen the whole way.
scenes.visual: The vesicle from the previous beat keeps drifting up to the plasma membrane. On 'fuses' it docks, the walls merge, and on 'opens to the outside' its teal interior spills open into the teal outside band; the vesicle membrane flattens into the plasma membrane and the protein ends up in it with the N ball and sugar flag on the outside, C ball in the gold cytosol. On 'faces the fluid around the cell' the ghost flag and '?' from the hook appear and merge into the real sugar flag, answered. On 'the whole way' the teal trail from ER to outside lights up once more.
scenes.narration: A secretory vesicle then fuses with the plasma membrane. Its lumen opens to the outside. The sugar now faces the fluid around the cell. It rode inside a lumen the whole way.

scenes.tts: Endocytosis can bring the protein back in. Now the sugar faces the endosome lumen. At no step did the C terminus leave the cytosol.
scenes.visual: The plasma membrane around the protein dimples in, as in the predict scene, and pinches off; the sac joins the teal endosome. Protein in the endosome wall: N and sugar inside (teal), C outside (gold). On 'At no step' a small strip of four mini-frames runs along the bottom (ER, Golgi, surface, endosome), each showing the green C ball on gold; a gold underline sweeps under all four.
scenes.narration: Endocytosis can bring the protein back in. Now the sugar faces the endosome lumen. At no step did the C terminus leave the cytosol.

scenes.visual: Show before tell: camera pulls back to the whole cell; copies of the protein fade in one by one in the ER, a Golgi sac, a vesicle, the plasma membrane and the endosome, each with N and sugar on teal and C on gold.

scenes.tts: So the cell chooses a protein's sides once, usually at the E R. After that, traffic only carries it from lumen to lumen. Secretory and endocytic lumens count as outside; traffic never flips proteins.
scenes.caption: So the cell chooses a protein's sides once, usually at the ER. After that, traffic only carries it from lumen to lumen. Secretory and endocytic lumens count as outside; traffic never flips proteins.
scenes.visual: Whole cell again with all compartments. The five protein copies from the previous beat sit in their membranes, gently bobbing. On 'once, usually at the E R' the ER copy pulses. On 'from lumen to lumen' a teal glow runs through the compartments in route order; on 'Secretory and endocytic lumens' every teal route space brightens together with the outside band. Gold specks keep drifting.
scenes.narration: So the cell chooses a protein's sides once, usually at the ER. After that, traffic only carries it from lumen to lumen. Secretory and endocytic lumens count as outside; traffic never flips proteins.

scenes.visual: End card over the softly glowing cell (gold specks keep drifting): 'Secretory and endocytic lumens count as outside; traffic never flips proteins.' (11 words).
